sections.h2: What one photo can stand in for
paras: It can stand in for many listing, social, and ad images that would otherwise need a new shoot, as long as the result still matches the item you ship.

A new listing needs more than one picture. A seasonal post needs a fresh setting. A supplier photo may not match the rest of the store. When a buyer must see stitching or the ports on a charger, your own close photo is still the safer file.
sections.alt: Hands open tan handbag on a sunlit desk beside a folded sweater.

paras: Decide the destination before you make the image. A marketplace main image is stricter than a social post.

A main image usually wants pure white and nothing extra. Later gallery images can show use, scale, or a close detail. On your own store, match the backdrop you already use so the grid stays tidy. Product photos come out square, which fits a product grid and a feed post.

sections.h2: How do I check a photo before it goes live?
paras: Put the image next to the product in your hand and compare color, shape, proportions, logos, and the number of parts.

Zoom in on labels, buttons, and edges. If something is off, do not hide it with a caption. Make the image again with a clearer sentence or a sharper source photo. Leave printed words, famous faces, and logos you do not own out of the request. The [Content Policy](/content) says what can be uploaded. Uploads and results stay in your account and are not shown publicly.
